The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Priorities

The manifesto establishes five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, breaking barriers to opportunity, and NHS reform.

## Economic Policy

Labour commits to fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. Corporation tax will be capped at 25%. The party pledges no increases to Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT.

Key economic initiatives include:
- A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) for industrial investment
- An Industrial Strategy Council on statutory footing
- Business rates reform in England
- A ten-year infrastructure strategy
- Planning system overhaul to enable 1.5 million new homes
- Rail nationalisation as contracts expire
- Skills England to coordinate workforce training

## Energy and Environment

Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will receive £8.3 billion. The target is zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through expanded wind, solar, and nuclear power. No new oil and gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing licences continue. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy efficiency upgrades.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubled CT/MRI scanners, 8,500 new mental health staff, and workforce planning. Social care will move toward a National Care Service with national standards.

Education measures include 6,500 new teachers, free primary school breakfast clubs, curriculum review, and ending private school VAT exemptions.

## Immigration and Security

A Border Security Command will replace the Rwanda scheme. Additional asylum caseworkers and a returns enforcement unit will be established. Work visa policy will link to domestic skills training requirements.

## Crime and Justice

Neighbourhood policing will be restored with new officers. Knife crime measures include youth intervention programmes and weapon bans. Violence against women receives dedicated resources including specialist rape units in every police force.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers will lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 applies to Lords members. Voting age drops to 16. Devolution will be strengthened with improved intergovernmental structures.

## Foreign Policy

NATO commitment remains central. The party seeks improved EU relations without rejoining the single market or customs union, including veterinary agreements and professional qualification recognition. Ukraine support continues.

# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes managing public finances to reduce national debt as a share of GDP while investing in infrastructure. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The party would reform capital gains tax, increase the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and introduce a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks. Employment reforms include creating a "dependent contractor" status for gig workers, higher minimum wage for zero-hour contracts, and expanded sick pay eligibility.

## Health and Social Care
The manifesto commits to 8,000 additional GPs to enable seven-day appointment guarantees, expanded NHS dentistry access, and mental health hubs in every community. Cancer treatment would begin within 62 days of referral. Social care would include free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard), and a cross-party commission on sustainable funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased Carer's Allowance and statutory respite breaks.

## Climate and Energy
Targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home insulation programme would prioritise low-income households. The party would remove restrictions on solar and wind development, maintain the fracking ban, and invest in energy storage. Water companies would face sewage discharge bans, a Sewage Tax, and transformation into public benefit companies.

## Housing and Planning
The manifesto targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through ten new garden cities and reformed land compensation rules. Renters would receive three-year default tenancies and no-fault eviction bans. Residential leasehold would be abolished. Local authorities could increase council tax by 500% on second homes.

## Education
Proposals include specialist mental health professionals in every school, above-inflation funding increases, and free school meals for all children in poverty. Teacher recruitment would be supported through independent pay review and funded training. A standing commission would reform qualifications, and maintenance grants would be reinstated for disadvantaged university students.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto would repeal the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme while establishing safe legal routes for refugees. Asylum seekers could work after three months. Work visa policy would transfer from the Home Office to relevant departments, with merit-based criteria replacing salary thresholds. The Youth Mobility Scheme would expand to age 35 with three-year visas.

## Political Reform
Electoral changes include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, and scrapping voter ID requirements. The Ministerial Code would become statutory. House of Lords reform would introduce democratic mandates. Donation caps would apply to political parties.

## International Relations
The party proposes a four-stage roadmap toward EU Single Market membership, beginning with veterinary agreements and culminating in formal membership application. Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP with Army cuts reversed. International development would return to 0.7% of national income. The manifesto supports Ukraine, advocates for Israel-Gaza ceasefire, and would recognise Palestinian statehood.
